clue.text: Causing one to be dependent on dress-making?

definitions.meaning: said of a drug or routine that breeds addiction
a habit is a garment, as a monk's or a riding outfit, so making one is forming a habit

explanation.surface: A puzzled look at whether sewing frocks could make someone reliant on it.
explanation.definitionFit: Something addictive creates a compulsion, and a habit is also clothing, so the question mark flags the punning second sense.

clue.text: It is used to cut chops on a wooden top

parts.note: to chop is to hack, so chops gives hacks

indicators.note: the top of a down entry's word is its first letter, so the opening letter of wooden is taken

explanation.surface: A butcher's tool that slices chops resting on a wooden board.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chops' looks like meat being cut, but it is the verb, giving HACKS; 'wooden top' supplies W.
explanation.definitionFit: A saw with a fine-toothed blade in a frame is a cutting tool for metal or wood.

clue.text: Tack to put on fat

definitions.meaning: in sewing, to fix with long loose stitches
in cooking, to spoon melted fat over a roasting joint

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both loose temporary stitching and moistening meat with dripping while it roasts.

clue.text: A minstrel dancing within the confines of the court

indicators.note: the letters of the words a minstrel move about as if dancing, giving a new order

explanation.surface: A travelling musician performing a jig inside the walls of a royal court.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Court' suggests a royal palace, but it is a tennis court, whose side strips are its outer boundaries.
explanation.definitionFit: The paired parallel lines along each side of a tennis court mark its edges for singles and doubles play.

clue.text: Video wrongly set, missing English poet

indicators.note: letters set out wrongly are put in a different order, and here the word for English is missing from the result

explanation.surface: A video recorder programmed incorrectly fails to capture an English poet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wrongly set' rearranges VIDEO, and 'missing' says the E that 'English' supplies is not in the poet's name.
explanation.definitionFit: The Roman writer of the Metamorphoses is one of the great classical poets.

clue.text: Lack of this quality could cost you the earth

definitions.text: Lack of this quality could cost you the earth

parts.words: Lack of this quality could cost you the earth
parts.note: the Beatitudes promise the earth as an inheritance to the humble, so without humility you forfeit it; 'cost you the earth' also means very expensive

explanation.definitionFit: Humble mildness is the virtue Jesus blesses in the Sermon on the Mount with the promise of inheriting the world.

clue.text: So-called specialised skill not by any means required

indicators.note: so-called signals that the word is as it is called, that is, spoken

parts.note: practical expertise is know-how

explanation.surface: Expertise of a particular kind is in no way needed for the job.
explanation.walkthrough: KNOW-HOW said out loud matches the dialect adverb, the K being silent.
explanation.definitionFit: A colloquial adverb meaning in no way, chiefly American and dialect usage.

clue.text: Indian sergeant had rival in mess

indicators.note: putting the letters of had and rival into a mess jumbles them

explanation.surface: In the army mess hall, a soldier dealt with a rival.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mess' sounds like the army dining hall, which fits a sergeant, but here it means a jumble.
explanation.definitionFit: A rank in the old Indian army equivalent to a sergeant in the British forces.

clue.text: It may be put on to improve a wooden appearance

definitions.text: It may be put on to improve a wooden appearance

parts.words: It may be put on to improve a wooden appearance
parts.note: reads like makeup for a stiff actor, but is a thin decorative layer of fine wood glued over cheaper timber; 'put on' also hints at a false front

explanation.definitionFit: A thin facing of quality wood applied over plain furniture to make it look better.

clue.text: Found a camp abandoned

parts.note: to found metal is to cast it in a mould
a camp is a faction or party, which is a side

explanation.surface: Someone stumbled upon a deserted campsite.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Found' looks like the past tense of find, but it is the metalworking verb meaning to pour molten metal into a mould.
explanation.definitionFit: Discarded or rejected; something thrown away is left behind, deserted.

clue.text: Gag in which the woman turns on the man

parts.note: he is the pronoun for a man

indicators.note: turns means the woman's name is flipped round end to end

parts.note: Eva is the Latin form of Eve, the first woman

explanation.surface: A joke in which a wife rounds on her husband.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gag' looks like a joke but means to retch; 'turns' flips the woman's name, and 'on' sets it after the man in this across entry.
explanation.definitionFit: To retch is to strain as if vomiting, and both verbs mean the same involuntary spasm.

clue.text: The woman who could come to Elisha

indicators.note: the letters of the prophet's name could come to a new word when rearranged

explanation.surface: A woman who might visit the prophet Elisha.
explanation.walkthrough: In Australian slang this word is a general term for a woman.
explanation.definitionFit: Australian and New Zealand slang for a girl or a female.

clue.text: Height above which white caps are always worn

definitions.text: Height above which white caps are always worn

parts.words: Height above which white caps are always worn
parts.note: white caps suggest hats or wave crests, but mean mountain peaks with permanent snow on them

explanation.definitionFit: The altitude on a mountain above which snow lies all year round.

clue.text: Maori woman has a husband in port, perhaps

indicators.note: in shows the article and the husband's letter are placed inside the drink

parts.note: port is a fortified wine, an example of the class

explanation.surface: A woman from New Zealand whose husband waits in a harbour town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Port' suggests a harbour, where a sailor's wife waits, but it is the drink.
explanation.definitionFit: The Maori and Hawaiian word for a woman or wife.

clue.text: Big sacrifice for a budding witch doctor possessing nothing

indicators.note: the witch and doctor together possess, that is hold within, the zero
budding means not yet full grown, so the witch's name lacks its last letter

parts.note: Hecate is the Greek goddess of witchcraft, so stands for a witch
MB, Bachelor of Medicine, is a doctor's degree
O, the zero, means nothing

explanation.surface: A big sacrifice made by a young trainee shaman who owns nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Witch doctor' reads as one phrase, but the witch and the doctor are separate pieces; 'budding' drops the witch's final E, leaving five letters.
explanation.definitionFit: In ancient Greece, a great public offering of a hundred oxen; hence any large-scale slaughter.

clue.text: One to defame a Lesbian, for example

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
to defame someone is to slander them

explanation.surface: Someone who would malign a gay woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lesbian' is capitalised as the inhabitant of the Greek isle of Lesbos.
explanation.definitionFit: A person from Lesbos lives on that Aegean island, an example of an island native.

clue.text: Star with a rock fixation

parts.note: suggests a celebrity obsessed with rock music; really the Greek princess chained to a sea rock, later set among the stars as a constellation

explanation.definitionFit: The mythical princess bound to a rock as monster bait gave her name to a constellation and galaxy.

clue.text: Quarters arranged in grounds on the Cam

indicators.note: in means the abbreviation goes inside the Cambridge grounds

parts.note: the Backs are the college lawns along the river Cam in Cambridge
ARR is the abbreviation for arranged, used in music credits

explanation.surface: Lodgings set up in the meadows beside Cambridge's river.
explanation.walkthrough: The Backs are the lawns behind several Cambridge colleges running down to the river Cam.
explanation.definitionFit: Soldiers' quarters are the buildings where troops are housed.

clue.text: Co-driver's position

parts.note: a navigator in rallying sits up front, but a nagging passenger who tells the driver what to do is said to drive from behind

explanation.definitionFit: A passenger who gives unwanted directions is a so-called rear-seat driver, hence where a co-driver sits.

clue.text: Girl the French mount on horse

parts.note: Mont Blanc is the great Alpine peak on the French border
H is slang shorthand for heroin, known as horse

explanation.surface: A girl climbs up on her horse, as French riders do.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mount' looks like getting on a horse, but it is Mont Blanc; 'horse' is heroin, H.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman's given name, a variant of Blanche.

clue.text: Admired notice about painter

indicators.note: about means the advert wraps around the artist's name

parts.note: an ad is a notice or advertisement
Gustave Doré was a French painter and illustrator

explanation.surface: A review praised a notice about an artist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About' looks like 'concerning', but it is a container signal; the painter is the French illustrator Gustave Doré, accent dropped.
explanation.definitionFit: To admire someone greatly is to worship or idolise them.

clue.text: Drove into dictator, incurring imprisonment

indicators.note: into means the word for drove goes inside the dictator

parts.note: Il Duce was Mussolini's title as Italian dictator
to drive a vehicle or business is to run it, so drove gives ran

explanation.surface: A tyrant was hit by a car and ended up in prison.
explanation.definitionFit: An old literary word for confinement or captivity.

clue.text: Jimmy Porter, for instance, exploding on the air

indicators.note: exploding blows the letters of on the air apart into a new order

explanation.surface: A character's rant blasting out over the radio.
explanation.walkthrough: Jimmy Porter is the angry young protagonist of John Osborne's 1956 play Look Back in Anger.
explanation.definitionFit: A protagonist lacking traditional heroic virtues, as the embittered Porter famously does.

clue.text: One who abominates a half hearted shopkeeper

indicators.note: half hearted means half of the double letter at the word's heart is removed

parts.note: a hatter is a shopkeeper selling hats

explanation.surface: Someone who loathes a shopkeeper who has no enthusiasm.
explanation.walkthrough: The middle of HATTER is TT; losing one of them halves the heart.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who detests or loathes something.

clue.text: Black rule in the margin

parts.note: B is the standard abbreviation for black, as on pencils
order is control or rule, as in law and order

explanation.surface: A black line ruled in the margin of a page.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Black rule' looks like a ruled line, but B and ORDER are separate pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: An edge or boundary, the strip around the outside of something.

clue.text: Garment some find hot in india

indicators.note: some means only a portion of the words find hot in India is taken

explanation.surface: Some people find a certain garment hot to wear in India.
explanation.definitionFit: A loincloth worn by Hindu men, wrapped around the waist and legs.

clue.text: Hauled up near Brighton

definitions.meaning: an old past tense of heave, as in a ship hauled to
a seaside town in Sussex, England, adjoining Brighton

explanation.definitionFit: The word is a nautical past tense of heave and also a south-coast English resort beside Brighton.

clue.text: A heavenly streaker

parts.note: a streaker is a naked runner, but here a body leaving a bright streak across the sky

explanation.definitionFit: An icy body orbiting the Sun trails a glowing tail across the night sky.

clue.text: It's stifling below — cease operations

parts.note: stifling weather is close, hot and airless
down means below, at a lower place

explanation.surface: It's oppressive downstairs, so the business shuts.
explanation.definitionFit: To shut a business or plant permanently is to stop trading.

clue.text: Short test question

parts.note: being short with someone is being cross, irritable
to test someone is to examine them

explanation.surface: A brief exam question.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Short' looks like brief but means bad-tempered.
explanation.definitionFit: To interrogate a witness from the opposing side in court is to question them closely.
